text:
Alex Chen: quick sync — pricing & quota policy for the Q3 roadmap. we need a decision on tier caps + overages before we greenlight the Dedicated upsell packaging.
Priya Patel: high-level options: (A) two tiers (Standard / Pro) with soft overage + invoice, (B) three tiers (Free / Standard / Pro) with hard rate-limits on Free and soft on paid. also consider token vs request-based quotas.
Jamie Ortiz: from finance POV we need predictable floor revenue. overage pricing should discourage heavy misuse but not block growth — recommend 1.5x unit price for overage + monthly cap = 2x committed spend. will run model later today.
Eric Wu: implementation constraints: we currently enforce per-key token-bucket at edge (nginx) + redis. soft overage means we continue traffic and bill; hard limit means 429. soft is easier but needs billing pipeline hooks.
Priya Patel: proposal draft: Free: 1 req/s, 50k tokens/month, hard; Standard: 10 req/s baseline, 2M tokens/mo, soft overage with alerting; Pro: 50 req/s, 20M tokens/mo, soft overage + negotiated cap. overage unit = $0.02/1k tokens * 1.5.
Eric Wu: rough infra notes: implementing soft overage requires meter -> billing-event stream consumed by charge-service. we have meter events going to kafka, but charge-service needs a new consumer + idempotency. estimate ~2w dev + 1w testing.
Priya Patel: also need burst rules: allow 5x short bursts for 10s windows for Standard/Pro, to handle chat UX. Free stays strict.
Jamie Ortiz: ok on 1.5x, but suggest a monthly hard cap option customers can opt into to avoid runaway bills (opt-in checkbox). also need credit/alert thresholds at 50/80/100% usage.
Sasha Morgan: legal flag: for Dedicated customers with committed contracts we must not auto-bill overages without explicit clause. add language to TOS + SOW. for public hosted API, we can bill but need 30d invoice terms for enterprise.
Alex Chen: launch criteria checklist idea: 1) rate-limit enforcement + soft-overage billing wired end-to-end, 2) console UI showing quota & alerts, 3) docs + email templates for overage notification, 4) legal language + billing ops runbook, 5) econ model signoff from finance.
Priya Patel: agree. can we make a minimum viable scope for the initial launch (MVP) — ship Standard/Pro only, Free stays but limited to developer preview? reduces legal complexity.
Eric Wu: MVP feasibility: yes if we reuse existing meter -> kafka -> charge pipeline and build consumer. rough tasks: prototype consumer (3d), quota service small changes (4d), console widgets (5d), e2e tests (3d).
Alex Chen: who owns what? Priya product lead, Eric eng owner, Jamie finance signoff, Sasha legal for contracts, cycles: target ship by 2025-12-08 (weeks out).
Jamie Ortiz: I'll deliver econ models + sample billing scenarios by EOD Friday.
Priya Patel: I'll draft the public pricing page + console copy.
Eric Wu: I'll spin up prototype consumer tomorrow and post logs to this thread.
deploy-bot: build 11789/ci passed for pricing-meter-consumer (jenkins link: https://ci.internal/build/11789) :white_check_mark:
Alex Chen: cool — quick decisions needed: (1) three-tier vs two-tier? (2) hard-free or soft-free? (3) overage cap policy? please vote with quick replies.
Priya Patel: vote: three-tier, hard-free, monthly opt-in hard cap for paid accounts. :thumbsup:
Jamie Ortiz: vote: two-tier (no free for GA), monthly opt-in hard cap, keep overage at 1.5x.
Eric Wu: vote: three-tier, hard-free, implement soft-overage for paid.
Sasha Morgan: legal: prefer two-tier to simplify terms, but can accommodate three if sales signs off.
Alex Chen: tally so far — mixed. going to run a quick async poll in #product later. for now I'll capture MVP: Standard & Pro GA; Free remains developer preview with hard limits. Priya to finalize copy and Jamie to confirm econ.
Priya Patel: noted. will update PRD & link it here.
Eric Wu: prototyping logs: attaching snippet below — quota consumer successfully emits billing.events for 1k-token batch.
```
{"event":"billing","key":"acct_123","tokens":1024,"plan":"standard","timestamp":1748201600}
```
Priya Patel: thanks — that log format looks good for charge-service consumer.
Alex Chen: next sync Monday 09:30 PT. leave action owners in comments. thanks everyone. :rocket:
